paper.title: CasSR: use a cleaner reference, then return to the input

claims.claim: The selected scene motivates the authors’ argument that a category-level prompt is too coarse for fine image structure. CasSR’s crop retains more plausible local detail, but a single favorable scene cannot establish that language guidance is generally inferior. Later prompt ablations in this same architecture are the relevant narrower test.

The image activation module supplies a preliminary reference. Both images are encoded, and weight-shared ControlNet extracts their features. The U-Net receives feature additions plus multiple attention in its upsampling blocks. Reference attention encourages detailed reconstruction; original-image attention is intended to correct reference artifacts. Frozen and trainable symbols identify what is optimized. The architecture provides an opportunity to correct errors, not a mathematical projection onto the true image.

On DIV2K, CasSR gives MUSIQ 68.6242 and MANIQA 0.4927. The next-best listed values are DiffBIR’s 67.0657 and 0.4580, so table-derived relative gains are about 2.32% and 7.58%, not the prose’s 3.82% and 7.05%. CasSR’s LPIPS 0.3225 trails SeeSR 0.3050 and HAT 0.3175; NIQE 3.6026 trails DiffBIR 2.9574. Thus “best or second best across all metrics” is too broad. On RealSR, LPIPS worsens to 0.3822 versus SeeSR 0.3034, despite MUSIQ improving 69.7639→70.4224. These rows support a perceptual-quality trade-off, not general fidelity superiority.

The selected CasSR output better separates the wing from surrounding rocks and preserves an eye-like structure in the highlighted region. This illustrates why original-image attention might matter. It does not give the frequency of such successes, and the metric failures in Table 1 prevent extending this example to a universal content-preservation claim.

Using SCEdit rather than LR as reference changes DISTS 0.1797→0.1531 and MUSIQ 63.4204→68.6242. ControlNet is competitive and better on some metrics, supporting flexibility of the activation stage. However, this tests two alternatives, not arbitrary restoration modules. There is an internal reporting discrepancy: the SCEdit LPIPS here is 0.3175, whereas Tables 1 and 3 list 0.3225 for the full model. Without an explanation, these should not be silently merged into one definitive value.

Removing multiple attention visibly reduces detail in these examples, while adding a caption introduces questionable feather/fruit texture. This is direct qualitative evidence for the proposed mechanism but not a numerical isolation of its average gain: the paper provides no corresponding complete quantitative attention-ablation table. The text-related variations also interact with guidance, so one cannot attribute every change to language alone.

Adding a caption changes MANIQA 0.4927→0.5057 and FID 30.7808→30.6618, but worsens LPIPS 0.3225→0.3280 and MUSIQ 68.6242→68.2996. Thus the table does not support “captions never help”; it supports mixed effects. Removing both generic description and CFG gives much lower MUSIQ 57.3091, but changes two factors together. The paper’s image-first perspective is useful without turning it into a universal rejection of semantic guidance.
